audits.title: 88 An audit of the quality of documentation during the end of life phase of older adults in acute hospital settings
audits.standard: BMJ Supportive & Palliative Care 'Guidance for completing End of Life Structured Judgement Review' quality indicators
audits.setting: Stroke and Acute Internal Geriatric Medicine services, Cork University Hospital

cycle1.result: Stroke vs AIGM: recognition of dying 92.9% (26/28) vs 94.1% (16/17); DNAR 100% vs 100%; escalation plan 84.6% vs 75%; risk of dying communicated to family 75% vs 59%; anticipatory medicines prescribed 94.1% vs 92.9%; spirituality documented 17.9% vs 5.9%; patient wishes 7.1% vs 0%.

audits.other_findings: Communication of risk of dying to the patient was 3.6% vs 0%; palliative care consulted in 14.3% vs 29.4%.
audits.citation: Plant R, O'Flynn F, Rubel M. 88 An audit of the quality of documentation during the end of life phase of older adults in acute hospital settings. Age and Ageing. 2023;52(Supplement_3). doi:10.1093/ageing/afad156.103.

audits.title: An Examination of EOL Trajectories and Audit of EOL Documentation In Patients Admitted Under the Department for Older Persons Services
audits.standard: Oxford Audit Assessment Tool for Care of the Dying (1–5 point scale)
audits.setting: Department for Older Persons Services, Mercy University Hospital, Cork

cycle1.result: Greater than 90% of patients had satisfactory, good or excellent end-of-life documentation.

audits.other_findings: One-third of deaths were acutely unwell, one-fifth followed a dwindling trajectory, 15% had known specialist palliative care needs and about 10% had an unexpected cardiac arrest.
audits.citation: Alcock M, Stanley E, McGrath K, O'Caoimh R, Maloney E, Timmons S, et al.. An Examination of EOL Trajectories and Audit of EOL Documentation In Patients Admitted Under the Department for Older Persons Services. Age and Ageing. 2024;53(Supplement_4). doi:10.1093/ageing/afae178.308.

audits.title: End-of-life care in hospital: an audit of care against Australian national guidelines.
audits.standard: ACSQHC Essential Elements for Safe and High-Quality End-of-Life Care, Elements 1-5 (ten variables)
audits.setting: One public and one private acute hospital, Melbourne; retrospective medical record audit of deceased inpatients

cycle1.result: 87.2% had a limitation of medical treatment; documented decision to provide end-of-life care in 81.1%; pastoral care involvement 41.6%; 33.1% of non-palliative care patients referred to specialist palliative care; end-of-life care pathway used in 51.1%.

audits.other_findings: Public (n = 320) and private (n = 132) hospitals differed; a written entry of poor prognosis preceded the end-of-life decision in 91.97% of cases.
audits.citation: Bloomer MJ, Hutchinson AM, Botti M. End-of-life care in hospital: an audit of care against Australian national guidelines. Aust Health Rev. 2019;43(5):578-584. doi:10.1071/ah18215. PMID: 30830856.

audits.title: Room to Improve: An Audit of In-Hospital End-of-Life Care for Oncology Patients in a Tertiary Cancer Centre in Ireland During the COVID-19 Pandemic.
audits.standard: UK National Quality Board validated instrument for care of the dying
audits.setting: National tertiary cancer centre, Cork University Hospital

cycle1.result: Risk of dying documented in 65.2%; palliative care involved in 77% and pastoral care in 10.6%; what mattered to the patient documented in 24.2%; quality-of-death score poor in 21.2%.

audits.intervention: Planned: end-of-life coordinator, communication checklist, expanded end-of-life committee including junior doctors, and regular audit.
audits.citation: Carroll HK, Broderick A, McCarthy O, Bambury RM, Power DG, Collins DC, et al.. Room to Improve: An Audit of In-Hospital End-of-Life Care for Oncology Patients in a Tertiary Cancer Centre in Ireland During the COVID-19 Pandemic. Omega (Westport). 2026;92(3):1153-1168. doi:10.1177/00302228231196620. PMID: 37670454.

audits.title: GRASP Workload Nursing Measurement System at end of life.
audits.standard: GRASP workload tool completion after every shift and agreement with the Comfort Measures Order Set documentation; target 90%

cycle1.result: GRASP compliance 66.6%; GRASP-documentation accuracy 60-70% (4 patient records, 15 shifts), below the 90% target.

audits.citation: Stilos KK, Long A, Cretu E. GRASP Workload Nursing Measurement System at end of life. Can Oncol Nurs J. 2020;30(4):317-320. PMID: 33165379.

audits.title: Improving the safety and quality of end-of-life in an Australian private hospital setting: An audit of documented end-of-life care.
audits.standard: Australian Commission on Safety and Quality in Health Care Essential Elements 1-5 for end-of-life care

cycle1.result: Communication that patient was dying: family 91%, patient 36%; specialist referral 68%; advance care directives 13%; resuscitation plans 92%; response to concerns 100%.

audits.other_findings: 997 deaths over the period; patient-centred communication and shared decision-making need improvement.
audits.citation: Saunders R, Seaman K, Glass C, Gullick K, Andrew J, Davray A. Improving the safety and quality of end-of-life in an Australian private hospital setting: An audit of documented end-of-life care. Australas J Ageing. 2021;40(4):449-456. doi:10.1111/ajag.12986. PMID: 34342382.

audits.title: An audit of perioperative end-of-life care practices and documentation relating to patients who died in a surgical unit in three Victorian hospitals.
audits.setting: Surgical units in three hospitals, Victoria

cycle1.result: Preoperative functional risk assessment documented in 5%; end-of-life discussions documented in 71%, but in 60% not until 48 hours before death.

audits.other_findings: 57% had a documented opportunity for farewell with family; palliative referrals occurred 1-2 days before death.
audits.citation: Keon-Cohen ZM, Story DA, Moran JA, Jones DA. An audit of perioperative end-of-life care practices and documentation relating to patients who died in a surgical unit in three Victorian hospitals. Anaesth Intensive Care. 2022;50(3):234-242. doi:10.1177/0310057x211032652. PMID: 35301860.
